quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: In poor weather, a tractor-trailer may take up to ____ percent longer to stop than in ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more time to stop than smaller vehicles. In poor weather, a tractor-trailer may take 25 percent longer to stop completely than it would in ideal driving conditions.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, other drivers must account for:

options.text: The longer stopping distance that large vehicles need.
The shorter stopping distance that large vehicles need.
The quieter noise of larger vehicles.
The higher speed of larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer stopping distance that large vehicles need.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where you can see traffic ahead. Do not position yourself where the truck blocks your view.

questions.question: Stopping distance does NOT depend on:

options.text: Your reaction time.
The time of day.
Your vehicle's brake condition.
Your vehicle's tire condition and type.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time of day.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed. The time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: Driving much slower than the speed limit is:

options.text: Illegal.
Smart.
Safe.
Optional.

questions.correctAnswerText: Illegal.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic creates danger. It blocks other drivers, forcing them to change lanes. The law prohibits driving so slowly that you block normal traffic flow.

questions.question: A sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph" means:

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have time to slow down before the speed limit changes.
You should drive 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: A "Reduced speed" sign tells you to slow down. If a new speed limit is shown on the sign, that speed limit begins right at the sign.

questions.question: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and drive at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to give stopped emergency vehicles space. If you cannot change lanes safely, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible. Always slow down and be ready to stop at emergency scenes.

questions.question: A bicyclist who breaks traffic laws:

options.text: Is allowed to because bicyclists do not have to obey traffic laws.
Can be ticketed.
Will always get just a warning from police.
Will have their bicycle taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: When an intersection is blocked by traffic, you should:

options.text: Move slowly until traffic moves.
Get as close as possible to the car ahead.
Wait outside the intersection until you can drive all the way through.
Honk your horn to make cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait outside the intersection until you can drive all the way through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if traffic is backed up on the other side and you cannot get completely through. Wait until traffic clears so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: Unless posted otherwise, the speed limit in business districts is:

options.text: 70 mph
55 mph
40 mph
25 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 25 mph
questions.explanation: The default speed limit in business districts is 25 mph. Follow posted signs if a different speed limit is shown.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light means:

options.text: Stop, look both ways, then go if the road is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection fast.
Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other, what should you do?

options.text: It is always safe to cross after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
After one train passes, check the other track for a second train before crossing.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: After one train passes, check the other track for a second train before crossing.
questions.explanation: When there are two railroad tracks next to each other, watch for a second train after the first one passes. Wait until you are sure no train is coming from either direction on either track before crossing.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.
Leave your transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: When parking on a downhill slope, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. If your car rolls downhill, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: What do regulatory signs do?

options.text: They are placed wherever there is present danger.
They tell drivers what they must or must not do.
They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
They warn drivers that they are approaching a school zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tell drivers what they must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular and white with black text. They tell drivers what rules they must follow in an area. They may show speed limits, say no passing or no turning, or clarify other driving rules.

questions.question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.
They always have the right-of-way.
They don't have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many crashes with motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians happen because drivers did not see them, even when looking. These users are smaller, move faster, and have weaker lighting than cars. Always watch for motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians to prevent collisions.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Go slowly while waiting for an opening.
Speed up faster than the traffic on the freeway.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match the freeway traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the freeway traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic so you can blend in smoothly and safely. You must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: What does a single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Opposite direction traffic and drivers cannot pass.
Opposite direction traffic and drivers can pass when safe.
Same direction traffic and drivers cannot pass.
Same direction traffic and drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Same direction traffic and drivers can pass when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Broken lines mean drivers can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: How much alcohol does your body process in one hour?

options.text: Three drinks an hour.
One drink an hour.
Two drinks an hour.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: One drink an hour.
questions.explanation: The average person's body processes about one alcoholic drink in one hour. Many factors affect how impaired someone becomes, including how much they drink, how fast they drink it, their body weight, food intake, and overall health.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a:

options.text: Solid red light.
Stop sign.
Yield sign.
Caution sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop and go when it is safe. A stop sign may also be posted at this location.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Use different routes.
Drive the same way as on dry roads.
Stay farther away from the car ahead of you.
Avoid bridges and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the car ahead of you.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the space between your car and the car ahead. Your car will need more time to stop than it would on dry roads.

questions.question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what can you do?

options.text: You can still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You cannot turn anymore and must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You don't have to turn in the direction the arrow pointed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow turns into a solid green light, you can still turn in the direction the arrow was pointing. But you must first let pedestrians and oncoming traffic go.

questions.question: You must pull over to the edge of the road and let an emergency vehicle pass:

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: You must pull over to the right and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights. This applies whether the vehicle is behind you or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: A single broken yellow line in the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. You can pass when it is safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You can pass when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You can pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads:

options.text: Always drive at the speed limit.
Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Drive closer to the car ahead of you.
Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction on slippery roads. Slow down and do not use cruise control.

questions.question: The Child Passenger Safety Law says children under age 8 and shorter than ____ must use a safety seat or booster seat.

options.text: 5 feet, 5 inches
5 feet
4 feet, 11 inches
4 feet, 9 inches

questions.correctAnswerText: 4 feet, 9 inches
questions.explanation: Children under age 8 and shorter than 4 feet, 9 inches must sit in a safety seat or booster seat. They must be in the back seat of the vehicle.

questions.question: A solid white line in the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. You can pass when it is safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You can pass when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. You cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks right away and as fast as possible.
Always stop before crossing.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to cross before a train comes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to any train before crossing railroad tracks, especially if there are no lights or gates. Do not cross until your whole vehicle can fit on the other side. Avoid shifting gears while crossing.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Go faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other cars.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up to match traffic. Turn on your signal, look for an opening, and merge when it is safe.

questions.question: A yellow and black diamond sign:

options.text: Warns you about road conditions ahead.
Tells you where cities and towns are.
Tells you about traffic laws.
Tells you about construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns you about road conditions ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black symbols or words on a yellow background. They alert you to conditions on or near the road.

questions.question: When you meet an oncoming vehicle on a narrow road, you must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the other vehicle at least half of the road.
Tell the other vehicle to pull over.
Turn on high beams so the other driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the other vehicle at least half of the road.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, give vehicles coming the other way at least half of the road. Both drivers need enough space to pass safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is near.
Look both ways as you cross.
Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must stop if traffic requires it.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with more than one lane in your direction, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to the lane you came from.
The lane marked with an arrow.
The middle lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the lane you came from.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane closest to where you came from. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: What happens to your field of vision when you drive faster?

options.text: It gets wider.
It gets narrower.
It makes it easier to see traffic on the sides.
It stays the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gets narrower.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the narrower your field of vision becomes. As you go faster, you see less on the sides. You must stay alert to dangers.

questions.question: Your vehicle takes longer to stop on which type of road?

options.text: Wet or icy roads.
Paved highways.
Roads at night.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wet or icy roads.
questions.explanation: Stopping takes longer on wet or icy roads. It also takes longer on roads covered with loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn to the right.
Double curve ahead.
Winding road ahead.
Pavement ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road ahead has many curves and turns.

questions.question: What are signs that show information about dangerous road conditions called?

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to hazards ahead. Follow warning signs for your safety. Ignoring them can cause accidents.

questions.question: What is the most important thing to do when driving through curves?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Your vehicle may be hard to turn at high speeds. Slowing down helps you keep control.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Turn the wheel too far in the other direction.
Turn your steering wheel toward traffic.
Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
Let go of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, stay calm. Steer toward the direction the skid is going.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A volunteer group is cleaning up the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
Children are playing ahead.
There is a pedestrian crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that workers may be on or very close to the road. Be extra careful in this area.

questions.question: What should drivers do when driving in bad weather?

options.text: Drive faster to get where you are going sooner.
Stay closer to the car in front of you.
Stay farther away from the car in front of you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: When driving on wet roads, increase the space between you and the car ahead of you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep going at your current speed.
You must stop ahead.
Do not speed.
A traffic signal is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A traffic signal is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you there is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Your body weight.
How much you drink.
How much time passes between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much alcohol you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Being physically fit or how well you can "hold your liquor" does not affect your BAC.

questions.question: You are turning onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line in the middle. You know immediately that:

options.text: You are on a two-way road.
You are on a one-way road.
The road is under repair.
You must stay to the left of the broken yellow lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a two-way road.
questions.explanation: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass slower traffic when it is safe.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, turn your steering wheel:

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, turn the steering wheel in the direction you want to go. As the vehicle straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: At an intersection with a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars tailgating.
Move when the vehicle ahead of you moves.
Look right first, then left, then right again.
Look left first, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left first, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because vehicles from the left are closer to you. Then look right, then left again to catch any vehicles you may have missed.

questions.question: The driver's left arm and hand are extended downward. This hand signal means the driver plans to:

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Start up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand point downward, they are signaling that they plan to stop. Adjust your driving if you are following them.

questions.question: If a transit vehicle is signaling to re-enter the main roadway after stopping, you must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.
Move to the left lane.
Yield.
Speed up to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any transit vehicle that is signaling to re-enter traffic. Change lanes, slow down, or stop to let the bus safely merge into traffic.

questions.question: Driving without proper liability insurance may result in:

options.text: No negative consequences.
Only a warning.
A fine.
Jail time.

questions.correctAnswerText: A fine.
questions.explanation: All vehicles must have liability insurance. Driving without it can result in fines, community service, and suspension of your license and registration.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, the first thing you should do is:

options.text: Firmly apply your brakes.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Apply your parking brake.
Pump your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: On a slippery road, first take your foot off the gas. If you need to slow down more, apply gentle, steady pressure to the brake pedal.

questions.question: When you park uphill on a street with a curb:

options.text: Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels sharply to the left, away from the curb. If your brakes fail, your vehicle will roll toward the curb, not into traffic.

questions.question: You are coming to an intersection with a flashing yellow light. You should:

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive carefully through the intersection.
Prepare to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means proceed slowly and carefully. Look both ways before entering the intersection.
